notes.decision: Variant spelling of ⲡⲉϫⲉϥ 'he said' (cf. ⲡⲧⲁⲭⲉ in glossary as Lyc 'he said'). Standard discourse-introducer in Kephalaia.

'That of the wind, that of the fire, and that of the water' — the three garments of the Living Spirit. ⲧⲁ- is the relational prefix (the-one-of). The triad wind/fire/water is the cosmological-elemental triplet by which the Living Spirit clothes himself for cosmic ordering, distinct from the five light elements.

Translated 'he subjected them' / 'he ordered them.' Likely Lyc reflex of ⲍⲱⲣⲡ̄ 'subject' or ϩⲣⲃ-related form. Context: after setting up all the works of the cosmos above and below, he then 'arranged/ordered' them. Tentative.

ⲕⲁⲕϥ ⲁⲍⲏⲩ = ⲕⲱⲕ ⲁϩⲏⲩ 'strip naked.' The damaged subject ⲡⲧ.. likely begins ⲡⲧⲏⲩ 'the wind' (first of the three garments donned in line 21) — fitting the elemental action: the wind strips the cosmos. Confidence on the subject is moderate.

Tentative. Possibly = ⲥⲱϩⲙ̄ 'rebuke' (cf. glossary ⲥⲉⲍⲙ̄) or ⲥⲁϩⲛⲉ 'command, ordain.' Context — after scattering them for purification — fits a verb of commanding or instructing. Translation 'he commanded' offered tentatively but rendered in coptic field unchanged.
'The X of the Zone.' ⲧⲁⲡ likely = 'tip, horn, edge, limit' (cf. Sah. ⲧⲁⲡ 'horn'). The zodiacal/cosmic Zone (already in glossary) has limits/tips/horns. Translated 'limits of the Zone.'

Translated tentatively as '...are released' — possibly a Lycopolitan stative/qualitative form of ⲃⲱⲗ 'release' with 3pl referent (cf. ⲃⲱⲗ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ in glossary). Could alternatively be a stative of ⲃⲱϣ 'be naked, stripped.' Etymology not certain.

Left untranslated as ⲥⲁⲕⲡⲟ — etymology unclear. Possibly compound of ⲥⲁⲕ 'draw, drag' + ⲡⲟ (perhaps a place- or action-noun ending). The 3sg.f possessive ⲡⲉⲥ- is clear; the noun is opaque. Flagged for parallel research.
Left untranslated. Etymology unclear. Possibly Lycopolitan reflex of ϩⲟⲣⲟⲧⲉ 'fear' (with regular ⲣ→ⲗ and ϩ→ⲍ), or related to ϩⲣⲟⲧⲉ. Flagged for parallel research.
